analysis_notes.source_text_summary: Torah #209 is a four-line teaching opening with the verse 'Prayers were instituted corresponding to the Tamid offerings' (Berakhot 26b). The Rebbe identifies a universal spiritual problem: every person accumulates evil prayers — prayers said for wrong reasons (the thief's prayer before breaking in, Berakhot 63). These evil prayers are called 'תְּפִלּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד' — the opposing prayers that disrupt proper prayer. The remedy is hachnasat orchim of a Torah scholar, because (1) the guest blesses (Berakhot 46), (2) the word אוֹרֵחַ (guest) is bechina of 'וְאֹרַח צַדִּיקִים כְּאוֹר נֹגַהּ' (the path of the righteous = shining light), (3) 'בְּרָכוֹת לְרֹאשׁ צַדִּיק' (blessings upon the righteous) = the 18 Amidah blessings (Zohar/Tikun), so through the guest the prayer is repaired. The teaching concludes by re-reading 'תְּמִידִין תִּקְּנוּם': the Tamid represents hachnasat orchim of Torah scholars, as established by the Talmud (Berakhot 10a: 'one who hosts Torah scholars is as if he offered the Tamid'). The Torah's entire argument rests on four bechina equations and one eitza: the eitza (hosting scholars → fixes prayer) is already in the dataset (edge 2876). The four bechina pairs are all new to the dataset.
structural_observations: The Torah is an exceptionally compact teaching: 4 lines, 1 eitza edge (already in dataset), 4 bechina declarations (none yet in dataset).

The word-play on א-ר-ח (aleph-resh-chet = guest/path) is the conceptual hinge of the entire teaching. The guest who comes to be hosted physically IS the righteous path spiritually — they share the same root word and the same essential nature.

The good/evil mirror structure is present in miniature: Package 1 (proper prayer and its blessings) vs. Package 2 (evil prayers that oppose them). The teaching moves from evil prayer [Package 2] through the eitza solution [hachnasat orchim] to restored proper prayer [Package 1].

The Tamid offering is the structural metaphor linking the Talmudic principle (prayers = Tamid) to the practical solution (hosting = Tamid). The Rebbe effectively rereads 'תִּקְּנוּם' as 'repaired' rather than only 'established', turning a historical fact (prayers were instituted) into a prescription (prayers can be repaired).

The 18 blessings of the Amidah are the explicit telos: the entire teaching is about restoring the capacity to pray the Amidah properly. The Zohar (Pinchas 244) and Tikun 47 are cited as the source for the equation of 'בְּרָכוֹת לְרֹאשׁ צַדִּיק' with the 18-blessing prayer.
